answer: A falcon does not trust a fable: it checks the hunt. Likewise, require every agent to periodically complete a fresh, time-boxed proof of useful work — a verifiable computation whose result only real hardware can produce in time. The work difficulty scales with how many identities one operator claims, like pigment darkening with each added layer, so cloning identities multiplies real compute cost while honest agents pay once. Forged answers fail verification and the identity loses its standing, making a Sybil farm pay full price for every fake.
